name: Sir Alex Ferguson
scopeNote: Re-research of Sir Alex Ferguson across the three counted spells (St Mirren, Aberdeen, Manchester United), tagged by era in each source's 'era' field: aberdeen-1978-86, united-1986-93, united-1993-2001, united-2001-06, united-2006-13, united-all (career-wide statements). Coverage: Aberdeen 1978-86 is THIN and mostly anecdotal on people-management and squad-building, with one StatsBomb-based match (1983 final); no formation, pressing or marking source beyond the Wilson 4-4-2 note. United 1986-93 has shape and counter-attack facts (Wilson, Tifo) but little else. United 1993-2001 has the 1999 midfield, the 1995 cull and the 2000 Real Madrid shift to caution (Wilson, SI). United 2001-06 is thin: Queiroz's defensive stance (Irish Times, FourFourTwo) and the Mourinho-driven three-man midfield. United 2006-13 is the best covered: Meulensteen's Coaches' Voice principles (pressing, block, possession, attack), Queiroz's 2008 Barcelona block (Carrick), Rooney on the 2009/2011 finals, the 2012/13 diamond and passing data. St Mirren 1974-78 has no tactical evidence. Style label: sources call it the 4-4-2 family (4-4-1-1 with a deep second striker, lop-sided with an inside winger), moving to 4-2-3-1 and 4-3-3 after 2000; Ferguson denied playing 4-4-2 (Wilson). The popular 'United Way / attacking counter-attack' label is disputed by FourFourTwo: it argues United mostly dominated with the ball and Ferguson was a pragmatist, not a philosopher. DATES FROM MEMORY or the v1 Wikipedia table, not re-checked here: St Mirren start 1974-10-01; St Mirren end/Aberdeen start (the Aberdeen appointment was reported on 1978-06-06 per FourFourTwo, v1 used 1978-06-01); Aberdeen end 1986-10-31 and United start 1986-11-06 (Wilson confirms first game Nov 1986); United end 2013-05-19 (last match, from memory; Gulf News 2013-05-09 and Meulensteen confirm 2013 exit). Queiroz's 2002 hire is also from memory. Rooney, Carrick and Meulensteen are retrospective witnesses. No Ferguson-specific set-piece or man-versus-zonal marking source was found.
openQuestions: Norwich 1993: Wilson reads the win as a counter-attack (Kanchelskis goal from McClair long pass) while the Tifo transcript, citing Michael Cox, reads it as a possession game in a 4-4-2. Both are single-match readings.

Possession versus counter-attack identity: FourFourTwo (Ruthven 2019) says United mostly dominated with the ball; Wilson and Tifo describe counter-attacks and soaking pressure against rivals; Queiroz's 2005 quotes push a defensive line. Probably era-dependent.
Credit for the post-2000 caution and the 2008 European setup is split between Ferguson (Wilson) and Queiroz (Carrick, FourFourTwo).
Rooney's 'suicidal' 2009/2011 criticism is one player's retrospective view; the 2011 preview blog also blames the 2009 4-4-2.

Set-pieces and marking (man versus zonal): searched twice, nothing Ferguson-specific found (the claim that he relied on man marking was a search summary only, not read). Eurosport 1999 treble piece (set-pieces section) and the Zonal Marking 2010 Liverpool piece were unreadable.
Should the file narrow to United 1993-2013? The Aberdeen and 1986-93 evidence is mostly one-off facts; most pressing/block/possession evidence sits in 2006-13.

sources.title: Sir Alex Ferguson was as adept at evolving tactically as any manager in history (Jonathan Wilson)
sources.evidence: The Aberdeen side that won the Cup Winners’ Cup final against Real Madrid in 1983, for instance, was set up in the lop-sided 4-4-2 familiar in Britain at the time with Gordon Strachan tucked in on the right side of midfield, Peter Weir as a more attacking winger on the left, and Eric Black dropping off the central striker Mark McGhee.

sources.title: Sir Alex Ferguson was as adept at evolving tactically as any manager in history (Jonathan Wilson)
